source.title_on_document: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation

supplement.where: Online Appendix, PDF pp. 30-54 (appendix pp. 1-25). Replication data and code are linked on PDF p. 3 at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32132980.
supplement.holds: Appendix A contains English translations of laboratory and rater instructions (PDF pp. 30-35), including explicit termination of ChatGPT access after the composition. Appendix B contains construction details and Python code for Idea request, Idea request index, and Similarity (PDF pp. 35-52). Appendix C Table 1 contains mediation SEMs using AI-first and User-first keywords (PDF p. 53); its references end on PDF p. 54. All creativity, character-count, and DAT treatment-contrast statistics extracted here are in main-text Tables 1, 2, and 5. Whether external replication files contain additional treatment-effect statistics is not established by this PDF; those files were not inspected.

paper_design_summary: At VERALabEx in Venice, the study analyzed 360 participants, primarily economics-related students, who wrote a creative composition in a between-subjects experiment crossing ChatGPT access with tournament, piece-rate, or lottery incentives. Four independent Italian-speaking Prolific raters, blind to treatment, scored each composition; analyses use each participant's mean rating and text length. A DAT word-association score was collected in the post-experimental questionnaire, after ChatGPT access ended.

studies.label: Lab experiment, 2 x 3 (AI access x incentive scheme), creative composition

participants.exclusions: No exclusions or attrition flow are reported. The paper states that the experiment was conducted with 360 participants and that participants were randomly assigned, but it does not give a count specifically at assignment. Thus n_randomized and all per-arm randomized counts remain null. Table 1 reports the analyzed cell counts; Tables 2 and 5 report 360 full-sample observations, with 148 No AI and 212 AI observations in Table 2. Unequal cell sizes are not explained. Absence of an exclusions statement does not establish zero exclusions.
participants.who: Participants at VERALabEx, primarily students in economics-related programs; Italian as first language required. Sessions included up to 20 participants (PDF p. 8); sessions are described as exactly gender-balanced (PDF p. 7, footnote 1).
participants.quote: The experiment was conducted at VERALabEx (Ca’ Foscari University of Venice) with 360 participants, primarily students in economics-related programs. Eligibility required Italian as a first language.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4.2, as named in the document, via API embedded in the oTree interface (PDF p. 7, Section 2.1; PDF p. 27, AI declaration).
ai_tool.how_used: Participants in AI arms could send free-form queries without restrictions on form or number during the composition; access ended when the composition was completed (PDF p. 7, Section 2.1; PDF p. 31, Appendix A.1). Table 1 reports AI (use), defined as sending at least one query: T&AI 0.818, PR&AI 0.677, L&AI 0.790 (PDF p. 14).

task.description: Short creative composition answering 'If you had the talent to create something simply with your thoughts, what would you create?' (PDF p. 6, Section 2.1). The suggested length was about 150 words, with no penalty for exceeding it (PDF p. 31, Appendix A.1). Experimental language was Italian (PDF p. 30, Appendix A; PDF p. 39, Appendix B.6). The later DAT elicited words and scored their semantic distance (PDF p. 14, Table 1 notes).
task.duration: Suggested no more than 15 minutes for the composition; explicitly indicative rather than enforced (PDF p. 31, Appendix A.1). Laboratory sessions lasted about 50 minutes (PDF p. 8, Experimental Procedures). DAT duration is not stated.

outcomes.name: Average creativity score (mean of four Prolific raters' scores of the composition)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Four independent Italian-speaking Prolific raters evaluated each composition; each rater evaluated four randomly assigned texts, blind to AI and incentive conditions, with each text appearing once in each position (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 2.2). The main outcome is the mean of the four ratings for each participant's single composition. Main text says a 1 to 10 scale (PDF p. 9); both laboratory and rater instructions say 0 to 10 (PDF pp. 32, 34). The actual minimum is unresolved. OLS analyses use participant-level mean scores with robust standard errors (PDF pp. 16, 23, Tables 2 and 5).

outcomes.measure_detail: Mechanical character count of the submitted composition, coded as elaboration (PDF p. 14, Table 1 notes). The measure code is null because the codebook supplies no category for character counts; automated_score specifically denotes a creativity-scoring model (creativity-codebook.md, Section 6). outcomes.name: Divergent Association Task (DAT) score, post-experiment questionnaire
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: DAT score is the average semantic distance, ranging from 0 to 100, between words supplied by one participant (PDF p. 14, Table 1 notes). It measures within-person associative variety, coded as flexibility under the codebook's explicit rule that variety among one person's own ideas is flexibility (creativity-codebook.md, Section 6). The measure remains automated_score. The paper treats DAT as baseline creative potential, but it was collected in the post-experimental questionnaire (PDF p. 8) after ChatGPT access ended with the composition (PDF p. 31). Table 5 column (3) estimates its association with randomized AI access and incentive indicators (PDF p. 23). Retained as a secondary after_ai outcome under the codebook timing rule; no delayed follow-up is reported.
outcomes.delay: Same laboratory session, in the questionnaire after the experimental stages; no elapsed delay is stated (PDF p. 8, Section 2.1).

eligibility.reason: All three criteria are met for S1: the abstract explicitly reports random assignment to ChatGPT access versus no access (PDF p. 3), and the methods confirm randomized treatments in a between-subjects laboratory experiment (PDF pp. 6-8, Section 2.1). Tables 1, 2, and 5 establish 360 analyzed writers across the six arms (PDF pp. 14, 16, 23). Independent raters scored the creativity of participants' compositions, produced while AI was available in AI arms (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 2.2; PDF p. 31, Appendix A.1). The unspecified individual versus session assignment unit and missing assignment-stage counts affect implementation and precision assessment, but do not overturn explicitly randomized AI access or the analyzed people count. Correcting the character-count measure and DAT construct does not affect the qualifying rated-creativity outcome.

one_line_finding: Among 360 analyzed participants, mostly students, ChatGPT access increased mean rated creativity by 0.398 points (robust SE 0.139; PDF p. 23, Table 5, column 1).
open_questions: Number randomized: no count specifically at assignment or participant-flow account is given; n_randomized remains null, and unequal analyzed arm sizes are unexplained (PDF pp. 8, 14, 16).

Assignment implementation: assignment.unit is null because the paper reports random assignment to AI treatments without specifying individual versus session allocation. References to sessions conducted under the tournament condition leave the implementation and any required session clustering uncertain (PDF p. 8; Appendix A.1, PDF pp. 30-32). Reported SEs are robust rather than explicitly session-clustered (PDF pp. 16, 23).
Actual rating-scale minimum: the main text says 1 to 10 (PDF p. 9), whereas both sets of instructions say 0 to 10 (PDF pp. 32, 34). The PDF does not reconcile them.
Rater payment currency: main text says 3 Euro (PDF p. 9), but rater instructions say 3 British pounds (PDF p. 34). The PDF does not establish which was paid.

Whether the external replication files include additional treatment-effect statistics cannot be established from the linked-data statement alone (PDF p. 3); only the full saved paper and bound appendix were inspected.
Identity and exact sample overlap of the separate Stage 2 competition-choice study are not given (PDF p. 8).
notes: Final review covered the complete markdown conversion, including references, all appendix instructions, Python code, and Appendix C, and checked the source passages and retained numerical statistics against PDF text. All three challenge problems were corrected. The assignment unit and character-count measure code are null because the source or codebook does not support a definite code. DAT is after_ai because AI had been removed; its construct is flexibility under the codebook's within-person-variety rule. All three output outcomes are retained. No outcome compares outputs across participants. Similarity compares each participant's composition with their own AI responses, so it is not across_people diversity (PDF p. 36, Appendix B.4). Idea-request measures describe prompting behavior; keyword-based mediation variants describe AI reliance. Tables 3 and 4 and Appendix C Table 1 do not add randomized AI-access outcome contrasts. The self-selected AI-use split in Table 2 column (2) is retained separately with comparison_type other. Table 2 column (3) reports AI -0.163 (robust SE 0.181) conditional on query count and its square (PDF p. 16); the text gives an implied maximum at approximately eight queries (PDF p. 15). These are analyses of self-selected interaction intensity and do not replace the randomized access contrast. Only cell-specific means and SDs are printed; pooled AI and No-AI means and SDs are not supplied. Table 5 column (1) is the preferred headline specification; Table 2 column (1) conditions on text length and post-experimental DAT. No effect sizes, pooled descriptive statistics, or missing counts were calculated. The external rating survey supplies measurement for the laboratory study and is not a separate randomized AI-assistance study. External replication files were not inspected. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as a historical record; final.challenge_resolution supersedes its DAT construct decision. The six final.open_items cover all open_questions and the three unresolved reconciliation differences; none affects eligibility.

open_items.item: Assignment-stage and per-arm randomized counts, attrition, and unequal analyzed arm sizes (open_questions[0]; unresolved reconciliation.differences on studies[0].participants.n_randomized): authors would need to supply assignment and participant-flow records. Criterion 2 is already met by 360 analyzed people (PDF pp. 14, 16, 23).

Individual versus session assignment and required SE clustering (open_questions[1]): authors would need to supply the treatment-allocation protocol and session identifiers. Criterion 1 is met by explicit random assignment to AI access (PDF pp. 3, 8); the missing implementation detail affects precision assessment.

Actual rating-scale minimum (open_questions[2]): main text says 1 to 10, while instructions say 0 to 10 (PDF pp. 9, 32, 34). Authors would need to confirm the administered rating instrument. Either scale supplies output-based creativity scores, so criterion 3 remains met.

Rater payment currency (open_questions[3]; unresolved reconciliation.differences on open_questions.rater_payment_currency): authors would need to confirm the actual payment, given 3 Euro in the main text and 3 British pounds in the instructions (PDF pp. 9, 34). This does not affect any eligibility criterion.

Additional treatment-effect statistics outside the saved PDF (open_questions[4]; unresolved reconciliation.differences on source.supplement.holds.external_completeness): inventory and inspect the linked replication data and code at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32132980 (PDF p. 3). All eligibility criteria are already supported by the saved PDF; this concerns extraction completeness.

Identity and exact analyzed overlap of the separate Stage 2 competition-choice study (open_questions[5]; PDF p. 8): authors would need to identify that paper and its analyzed participant set. This concerns sample deduplication, not any eligibility criterion for S1.
